Winding Back the Years

By Alma Rutkowski

The annual Antique Clock and Watch Fair was held this weekend at the Merrow Assembly Rooms, drawing collectors from every part of the country. This year’s fair displayed pieces made between the 1780s and the 1930s. – [1] –.

The fair also featured a presentation on a joint project involving several local workshops that had come together to restore an 1890s tower clock. Each workshop took charge of one element of the mechanism, such as the dial or the escapement. – [2] –.

One of the highlights was a talk by Emil Bergström of the Northern Horological Society. – [3] –. Based on decades of experience repairing the mechanisms inside clocks, he described the slow business of tracking down rare components and the patience needed to bring a seized movement back to life. – [4] –.
